description: Door and turnstile access for tenants and staff; issuing and revoking cards and mobile credentials; door schedules and after-hours access
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Doors must lock and unlock on schedule; door controllers cache credentials for up to 72 hours, but no credential can be issued or revoked while the cloud platform or a property network is down. A revoked credential that still works is a physical security exposure. Officers can staff main entrances for one shift before overtime and fatigue limits are reached
manual_workaround: Officers post at main entrances with printed tenant lists; perimeter doors set to scheduled lock; turnstiles to card-only; credential changes queued on paper and entered on recovery
dependent_systems: SYS-02; SYS-04; SYS-05; SYS-09 (console PCs); SYS-14 (mobile credentials)
dependent_third_parties: Access control and video platform vendor; access control and video integrator; SD-WAN provider; ISPs
dependent_people_or_facilities: Director of Security Operations; SCC operators; 162 security staff; lobby desks at Towers 1-4 and Mixed-Use 1-2
quantified_operational_impact: About 410 door controllers, 2,300 readers, and 36 turnstile lanes; about 14,500 credential holders; about 120 credential changes per business day cannot be made; about 60 entrances to staff by hand
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: Lease security obligations; 31 tenants with 72-hour notice clauses if tenant employee data is exposed; Fla. Stat. 501.171 if personal information is accessed
occupant_safety_impact: Severe: unsecured entrances at occupied buildings. Emergency egress is not affected (door releases are hardwired to the fire alarm)

business_process: Building environmental control on BAS Platform A
description: Supervisory control and alarm handling for chillers, cooling towers, air handlers, VAV boxes, lighting schedules, and meters at the towers and mixed-use properties
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Field controllers keep their last programs, but nobody can change setpoints, answer chiller or air handler alarms, or run after-hours HVAC. In the Florida climate, tower floors and tenant data rooms overheat within one business day. Manual rounds on 18 to 32 floors need every engineer on site; crews tire after about 12 hours. Office leases on the 2024 template allow rent abatement after 3 consecutive business days of untenantable premises. RPO 24 hours matches the rate of program changes
manual_workaround: Chief engineers switch plant equipment to local hand control and run hourly rounds; portable cooling for tenant data rooms; lighting on local switches; after-hours HVAC by request to the engineer on duty
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (Platform A); SYS-04; SYS-08 (historian, backups, remote access gateway); SYS-09 (engineering tablets)
dependent_third_parties: BAS Integrator A; equipment service contractors; SD-WAN provider; portable cooling rental vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: VP of Engineering; Building Technology Manager; 6 chief engineers; about 130 engineering staff at Towers 1-4 and Mixed-Use 1-2
quantified_operational_impact: About 5,200 field controllers and 52 chillers and air handlers per day of rounds; 6 properties and about 9,800 tenant employees affected
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: Rent abatement exposure from day 4 (2024 office template; about 60% of office rent); 2 JV properties (Tower 3, Tower 4) report outages to the JV partner within 2 business days under the management agreement
occupant_safety_impact: Moderate: heat stress for occupants and data room equipment failure; life-safety systems are separate and unaffected

business_process: Building environmental control on BAS Platform B
description: Supervisory control for rooftop units, air handlers, parking and site lighting, and meters at the retail centers and office parks
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Rooftop units run on local schedules; most retail tenants control their own space temperature. Site and parking lot lighting schedules are on the BAS and matter for evening safety. Retail leases allow abatement after 5 business days, office park leases after 3
manual_workaround: Local hand control of rooftop units; site lighting on photocell override; engineers on extended rounds; guard patrols in parking fields after dark
dependent_third_parties: BAS Integrator B; HVAC service contractors; ISPs
dependent_people_or_facilities: 8 chief engineers; about 70 engineering staff at Parks 1-2 and Retail 1-6
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,600 field controllers and 8 site servers; 8 properties; about 170 retail tenants
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: Retail co-tenancy and abatement claims after 5 business days; office park abatement after 3 business days
occupant_safety_impact: Moderate: dark parking fields and walkways after sunset if lighting schedules fail

business_process: Security Command Center (SCC) monitoring and video surveillance
description: Live monitoring of about 3,400 cameras, door alarms, and BAS critical alarms for all properties; incident dispatch; video requests from police and tenants
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The SCC is the only place that sees all 14 properties. Without it, door-forced alarms and BAS critical alarms go unanswered and officers are dispatched by radio only. Backup console positions at Tower 3 have never run a full shift. Video retention (14 to 90 days) is evidence for police and insurers
manual_workaround: Officers on increased patrols; property desks watch local NVR clients; radio dispatch; BAS critical alarms phoned to chief engineers
dependent_systems: SYS-03; SYS-02; SYS-04; SYS-09 (40 console PCs); SYS-05
dependent_third_parties: Access control and video platform vendor; access control and video integrator; guard contractor
dependent_people_or_facilities: SCC operators (6 positions, 24x7); security officers; Tower 1 SCC room and Tower 3 backup positions
quantified_operational_impact: About 3,400 cameras and 46 NVRs; about 70 door-forced or held alarms and 15 BAS critical alarms per day go to the SCC
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: Video evidence requests from law enforcement and insurers; lease security service obligations
occupant_safety_impact: Severe: delayed response to incidents involving occupants

description: Building notices, emergency and weather instructions, and service interruption notices to tenant contacts and occupants by tenant app push, SMS, email, and phone tree
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: During any building systems outage or hurricane event, tenants must get instructions quickly. In-building emergency voice systems are separate (SYS-13), but occupant-wide notices outside an alarm event depend on the tenant app and email. Lease clauses require prompt notice of service interruptions, and 31 tenants have 72-hour notice clauses for data incidents
manual_workaround: Phone tree to tenant contacts from printed lists kept by each Property Manager; lobby signage; floor wardens; text messages from Property Managers' company phones
dependent_third_parties: Tenant experience app vendor; productivity suite vendor; mobile carrier
dependent_people_or_facilities: VP of Property Management; 10 Property Managers; Director of Marketing and Communications
quantified_operational_impact: About 420 tenant contacts and 9,800 app users; about 40% of printed tenant contact entries are more than 12 months old
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: Lease notice clauses; 72-hour clauses in 31 leases
occupant_safety_impact: Severe: occupants do not receive instructions during an emergency outside the fire alarm system

description: Registering visitors, scanning ID, printing passes, and turnstile passes at lobby desks
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Lobbies can run on paper logs with officers checking ID, but entry slows for about 1,100 visitors a day and tenants complain within hours
manual_workaround: Paper visitor log; officer escort; tenants pre-register by email to the lobby desk
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,100 visitors per business day; manual check-in takes about 3 times longer
occupant_safety_impact: Moderate: less control of who is in the building

business_process: Engineering work orders and tenant service requests
description: Tenant requests, preventive maintenance, after-hours HVAC requests, and contractor dispatch
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 300 new requests per business day can be taken by phone; preventive maintenance can slip a few days
manual_workaround: Phone and email requests to each management office; paper work orders entered later
dependent_third_parties: Property management system vendor; tenant experience app vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 300 new requests and 1,100 open work orders per business day
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: Preventive maintenance records support insurance and warranty claims

business_process: Tenant experience app and mobile credentials
description: Mobile credentials, amenity bookings, building notices, and service requests for about 9,800 app users
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 6,200 tenant employees use only mobile credentials. If the app or its integration fails, they need temporary cards at the lobby desk. Notices fall back to email and phone (BP-05)
manual_workaround: Temporary cards issued at lobby desks from the access control platform; amenity bookings by email
dependent_third_parties: Tenant experience app vendor; access control and video platform vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 6,200 mobile-only credential holders; about 4,000 temporary cards needed per business day at peak
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: Personal information of 9,800 users under Fla. Stat. 501.171 if breached (names with account credentials)

business_unit: Parking (6 garages, operated by the parking operator)
description: Garage entry and exit, monthly permits, transient parking revenue, and license plate recognition for permits
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: If gates or the revenue system fail, the operator raises the gates and parking is free; the company's revenue share is lost for the period. Monthly parkers and tenant parking ratios are lease obligations
manual_workaround: Gates up; operator staff verify monthly permits by sticker; cash-free exits counted for reconciliation
dependent_systems: Parking operator systems (outside company systems); SYS-04 (garage network at 2 mixed-use properties)
quantified_operational_impact: About $26,000 of gross parking revenue per day across 6 garages (company share about $4,400)

business_process: Rent billing, collections, and tenant accounting
description: Monthly rent and recovery invoices, ACH collection, receivables, CAM reconciliation, and JV accounting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $8.3 million billed each month, mostly collected in the first 5 business days. A delay at month start moves cash, not revenue. The SaaS vendor holds its own backups. JV and lender reports have monthly deadlines
manual_workaround: Invoice from the prior month's register; tenants pay by bank transfer; credit line
quantified_operational_impact: About $8.3 million billed per month; up to about $6.5 million of cash delayed if the outage falls in the first week of a month
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: JV partner monthly reporting; lender covenant reporting

business_process: Accounts payable, treasury, and debt service
description: Vendor payments, payroll funding, debt service, and bank transfers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Debt service of about $3.1 million a month is due on fixed dates; vendor payments can slip a few days; bank portal access is separate from company systems
manual_workaround: Bank portal payments from a clean laptop with dual approval; manual check run
quantified_operational_impact: About $3.1 million of debt service per month; about 1,400 vendor payments per month
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: Loan agreements: late payment defaults and lender notice

description: Conference and event bookings, after-hours HVAC charges, badge replacement fees, and kiosk license fees
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 16,000 card transactions a year; customers can pay by invoice or ACH
manual_workaround: Invoice the customer; take payment later on a working P2PE terminal (never on paper)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Management office and conference center staff
quantified_operational_impact: About 44 card transactions per day across 6 offices
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: PCI DSS v4.0.1 by contract with the acquirer

description: Prospect tours, lease drafting, critical dates, and lease abstracts
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No same-day dependency; lease critical dates are tracked monthly
manual_workaround: Work from signed lease copies in cloud file storage
dependent_third_parties: Property management system vendor; lease abstraction AI vendor
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: Missed critical dates (options, notices) if outage spans a deadline

description: Monthly and quarterly reports to the JV partner and lenders from the data warehouse
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Reports are monthly; deadlines are about 15 business days after month end
manual_workaround: Reports built from property management system exports
quantified_regulatory_contractual_impact: JV management agreement and loan agreement reporting deadlines

description: Time capture, biweekly payroll for 600 employees (about 374 hourly security and engineering staff), onboarding, and terminations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; a missed payroll has legal and retention impact for hourly staff
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; paper timesheets
quantified_operational_impact: About $1.6 million of payroll per pay period

description: BAS historian, energy analytics, the AI energy optimization service (AI-004), and submetered utility billing to tenants
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Optimization saves about 6% of tower energy cost; submeter bills are monthly
manual_workaround: Run the BAS on fixed schedules without optimization; estimate submeter bills from prior months
quantified_operational_impact: About $1,500 per day of energy savings lost
